items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: He would call, I'd say, 'Man, what you calling me this -- say, your time is different.' ... He would call, I'd say, 'Man, call me back later. I can't talk now.' So he'd call my wife, say, 'Hey, Mil, wake him up.'

ctx.x: Duke called me Sonny lots of times but when he wanted something important, hey, Nasty. Even when he wrote the book, "Music is my Mistress", he used to call me 3:00, 4:00 o'clock in the morning to recall instances 20 years ago. I'd say, "Man, call me back later. I can't talk now." So he'd call
my wife, say, "Hey, Mil, wake him up." I'd say, Oh, God. But he understood. I would come up with names.

Like his first show, the Las Vegas time and New York time is different. He would call, I'd say, "Man, what you calling me this -- say, your time is different." I'd say, "Don't call me, Man." He would ask me, "What was that guy's name in Washington or New York, 20 years ago?" I'd say, "Call me tomorrow and I'll tell you." He'd call and I'd have it right on the nose. He knew I'd remember, you know.
